title: The critic who asked Lester for Bud Freeman records
summary: A critic who refused to play Freeman's records hosted Lester Young, who asked 'You got any Bud Freeman?'; years later the critic apologized.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, now, I am going to tell you a story that may sound to many people to be egomaniacal and God knows, I don't mean it in this sense, because I would like to try to live a gracious, humble sort of life if I can, and I don't always succeed with that. Evil gets ahold of all of us.

But this is a beautiful story about Lester Young. There was a critic whose name I shall not mention. Back some 30 years -- let's see if I am right, we are going into '78, so, yes, -- who refused to have a Bud Freeman record in his home. He loathed my playing and he idolized Lester Young. Now, he had invited Lester to his home for supper. His idol. And he wined and dined him and now, after dinner, he said, 'Would you want to come into my music den, I would like to play some records for you.'
They get in there and he gives Lester a cigar and some brandy and black coffee and he said, 'Lester, what would you like to hear?' And Lester said, 'You got any Bud Freeman?'
Now, I have to tell this story only because the

interesting ending of the story is this: that just a few years ago, I was to meet that same critic in London and he volunteered to tell me this story. Just some five years ago. I was over here on tour with the World's Greatest Jazz Band. He said, Bud, I owe you both a compliment and an apology, and he told me the story as I told you, He Said, I wouldn't have a Bud Freeman record in my home and when Lester Young said that, you got any Bud Freeman, it changed my whole attitude, and I said, Well, you didn't have to tell me that but that was very gracious. You have your right to dislike players as we all do, and what are all these things based on but opinion anyway.

So I learned one thing from that, Helen, that people have to be told what is good. A critic idolizes a certain artist and that artist can get away with murder. He can tell that critic that some non-entity is a genius and the critic will have to believe it.
